column1: # Which guards `scripts/dead-guard-scan.py` measures, and which it CANNOT.
# Keyed on the git REMOTE SLUG, never the clone directory name: two of the four
# clones are named nothing like their repo (`datapacket-talos` -> civitai/talos-infra,
# `homelab-talos` -> ZacxDev/homelab-infra), so a basename key silently matches the
# wrong profile or none at all.
# 🔴 THE `out-of-instrument` ROWS ARE THE POINT, NOT PADDING. A guard absent from
# this file would read as "measured and clean". These rows say, in the artifact
# itself, which ~180 of the ~270 guards this tool does not see and why. Removing a
# row does not extend coverage; it only hides the gap.
# 🔴 THE `instrument` SELECTORS NAME CORPUS-SCANNING GUARDS, NOT "the test
# suite". An earlier draft selected all ~110 `scripts/tests/test_*.py`; that
# instrumented ordinary unit tests, whose untaken branches are not the defect
# this tool looks for, and the traced run had not finished after 35 minutes.
# Narrow selectors are what make the flag list readable AND the run affordable.
# status:
#   instrument         -- traced; branch bodies with no executed line are flagged
#   out-of-instrument  -- NOT measured; the selector column states why
#   exclude            -- subtracted from an `instrument` glob before tracing
# 🔴 `exclude` IS THE ONLY STATUS WHOSE SELECTOR IS PARSED. Its shape is
# `<path-glob> -- <reason>`, the glob half is validated at LOAD time against a
# narrow character class (no spaces, commas, colons, absolute or `..` segments)
# and a malformed row is a hard SystemExit, not a warning. The
# `out-of-instrument` column stays ENGLISH -- `scripts/check-*.sh,
# kustomize-validate.sh: same bash line-granularity limit` is a sentence, and
# retroactively reading those rows as path patterns would silently change what
# four repos measure with nothing in the diff to show it. That is why exclusion
# got a new status instead of a new reading of an old one.
# 🔴 AN `exclude` ROW IS NOT AN ERASURE. Every file it removes is written into
# the census as an `excluded` row carrying this reason, because an exclusion
# makes the flag list shorter and a shorter list is indistinguishable from a
# cleaner repo unless the subtraction is in the artifact too.
# repo_slug<TAB>lang<TAB>status<TAB>selector_or_reason

column1: # 🔴 FOUR FILES THE GLOB ABOVE SWEEPS UP THAT PYTEST CANNOT COLLECT. They are
# named test_*.py and live in scripts/tests/, and they are not pytest modules:
# they are standalone procedural harnesses that shell out to docker and need
# network, they define no test functions, and they end in sys.exit(...). Their
# real callers are direct invocation (VETR_API_DIR=... python3 <file>) and
# scripts/tests/run-ci-suite.sh, which drives .py files one at a time through
# `python3 -m unittest discover`; for BOTH of those a module-level sys.exit(0)
# on "no target configured" is the correct do-nothing guard. Those files are
# CORRECT -- the defect was here, in a glob that assumed pytest-collectability.
ZacxDev/homelab-infra
column4: scripts/tests/test_vetr_ci_*.py -- standalone docker/network integration harnesses, not pytest modules: no test functions, they sys.exit() when done, and test_vetr_ci_bootstrap_guard.py calls sys.exit(0) at MODULE level when VETR_API_DIR is unset. Under pytest that SystemExit during collection is an INTERNALERROR which aborts the entire session (`no tests ran`, rc=3), so including them traced NOTHING and published 44 flags off a run that never executed a line. Driven instead by scripts/tests/run-ci-suite.sh via `python3 -m unittest discover`, one file at a time
